title: How Mixx Technologies Is Lighting The Way To Fully Optical Scale-up Networks
gist: Photonics startup Mixx, founded in 2023 by ex-Intel/Broadcom optics engineer Vivek Raghuraman and Rebecca Schaevitz, is starting with SxC, a 64-fiber connector, because scale-up fabrics like Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL576 could need around 20,736 fiber pairs. Its roadmap runs to near-packaged optics in 2028-2029, co-packaged optics around the end of the decade, high-radix optical circuit switches and a software control plane. The goal is a fully optical, SerDes-free, high-radix scale-up fabric that can drop packet switches.

themes.theme: Fiber density as the first bottleneck

insights.claim: As AI scale-up domains grow beyond copper-based racks like Nvidia's NVL72, optics become unavoidable, and the number of fibers to attach becomes the first problem; Mixx's first product, SxC, packs 64 fibers into a single connector.
insights.so_what: Dense fiber connectivity is an early-stage bottleneck and opportunity in optical scale-up.
insights.locator: Modern rack systems like Nvidia's NV72
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: Mixx co-founder Vivek Raghuraman says the company can fit 1,000 fibers within 800mm2.
insights.so_what: A concrete density metric to compare fiber-attach vendors.
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: The Next Platform estimates that, assuming one fiber pair per SerDes, Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL576 would need about 20,736 fiber pairs to connect its eight NVL72 racks, or 2,592 per rack, and even 16-wavelength DWDM would leave a lot of fiber to clean and terminate.
insights.so_what: Optical scale-up will drive large volumes of fiber, connectors and termination.
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: Nvidia's Vera Rubin Ultra systems expand NVLink Switch fabrics from 72-144 GPUs to 576 and eventually 1,152 GPUs using optics between racks, while communication within each rack stays copper.
insights.so_what: Nvidia's roadmap creates real demand for inter-rack optics in scale-up.
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: Any company building optical scale-up networks, whether AMD, Nvidia, or Broadcom's and Marvell's XPU customers, will need denser fiber attach, which is why Mixx is focusing on the connector first.
insights.so_what: Mixx's connector is vendor-agnostic, giving it a broad customer base.
insights.locator: This is the exact reason why Raghuraman
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

themes.theme: Pragmatic path from NPO to CPO

insights.claim: Mixx is building a three-part roadmap for optical scale-up networks: near-packaged and co-packaged optical engines, optical circuit switches, and a software control plane.
insights.so_what: A full-stack approach to optical scale-up rather than a single component.
insights.quote: It’s a three-pronged roadmap that we are developing to enable optical scale-up networks.
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: Mixx plans its first near-packaged optics (NPO) engine for GPU nodes in 2028 or 2029, because NPO is safer than co-packaged optics: a failed optical engine does not make the GPU useless and can in theory be refurbished.
insights.so_what: NPO is likely to be adopted before CPO in GPU systems.
insights.locator: NPO is generally seen as the safer option
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: Raghuraman expects Mixx's first co-packaged optics product around the end of the decade, when SerDes is no longer viable for scale-up networking, after the approach is proven in NPO form.
insights.so_what: Times the CPO adoption curve for scale-up to ~2030.
insights.locator: Raghuraman expects Mixx's first CPO product
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: Mixx's strategy is to time product releases to hyperscaler market demand rather than shipping proofs-of-concept years too early, a mistake that has plagued many photonics startups; Raghuraman previously led silicon photonics work at Intel for seven years and helped develop Broadcom's co-packaged optical switches.
insights.so_what: Team pedigree and demand timing reduce the execution risk typical of photonics startups.
insights.quote: We are not just making solutions that are proof of concepts, but something that can be deployed by the hyperscalers
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

themes.theme: Escaping SerDes limits and raising radix

insights.claim: At 400 Gbps a signal can travel only about 1.25 meters over copper without degrading, and each doubling of data rate halves the reach, while co-packaged optics only needs the electrical signal to reach an optical engine a few millimeters away.
insights.so_what: Rising lane speeds steadily push the copper-to-optics transition.
insights.quote: Double the data rate, halve the reach.
insights.locator: Where we're going, we don't need SerDes
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: Single-layer scale-up fabric size is limited by accelerator radix; Nvidia's Blackwell had 36 200 Gbps links, two to each of NVL72's 18 NVSwitch ASICs, and Raghuraman expects dropping SerDes to enable far higher radix approaching die-to-die interconnect densities.
insights.so_what: Higher radix from optics could change scale-up architecture and the role of switch silicon.
insights.locator: How large a single layer scale-up fabric
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: With enough ports per chip, scale-up fabrics might not need packet switches at all, improving latency, though Raghuraman says packet switches will still play a role in larger clusters at a higher network layer.
insights.so_what: A potential long-term threat to scale-up packet switch ASIC demand.
insights.quote: If we can avoid packet switching, it improves latency
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

themes.theme: Switchless fabrics and optical circuit switches

insights.claim: Google TPU and Amazon Trainium2 pods used switchless torus topologies due to limited radix, but toruses need more hops and suit mixture-of-experts models poorly, which is why AWS moved to a switched fabric like Nvidia's NVL72 for Trainium3.
insights.so_what: MoE models favor all-to-all fabrics, shaping accelerator network design.
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: Mixx is developing a high-density optical circuit switch because current OCS appliances lack density; Raghuraman says most are 16x16 or 32x32, and while Coherent and others offer hundreds of ports, those appliances are enormous.
insights.so_what: High-radix OCS is an unmet need in optical scale-up.
insights.quote: The biggest challenge with OCS today is getting high-radix OCS switches.
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann

insights.claim: OCS reconfiguration drops connections, so Mixx also needs a software control plane to schedule changes; in all-to-all fabrics these blips are less disruptive because multiple paths exist between accelerators.
insights.so_what: Software is a necessary, often underestimated part of optical fabrics.
insights.locator: It's also going to need a software control plane
insights.speaker: Tobias Mann
